java.toolchain: Java 27 (OpenJDK 27 at $JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/jdk-27; `java`/`javac`/`jar` are on PATH). Build with plain `javac`/`jar` from the Makefile or with Maven (`mvn`, offline; plugins already cached may be used, but no dependencies). Target release 27.
java.stdlib_note: The JDK (java.*, javax.*, jdk.* modules incl. com.sun.net.httpserver, java.util.concurrent, java.nio, the Foreign Function & Memory API and the incubating Vector API) is the standard library. JUnit is NOT available: write tests with plain Java (e.g. a small test main) or `assert`.

clojure.toolchain: Clojure 1.12.3 via the `clojure`/`clj` CLI and tools.deps (deps.edn), running on OpenJDK 27 ($JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/jdk-27). The only allowed dependency coordinate is org.clojure/clojure itself (already in the local Maven cache; there is no network).
clojure.stdlib_note: clojure.core and the namespaces shipped inside the Clojure jar (clojure.string, clojure.set, clojure.java.io, clojure.test, clojure.walk, clojure.edn, …) plus the entire JDK via Java interop are the standard library. NOT allowed: clojure.data.json, data.csv, core.async, http-kit, ring, cheshire or any other library outside the Clojure jar.

rust.toolchain: Rust 1.96.0 stable with Cargo (offline; `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`). Use edition 2024. Release builds for the launcher.
rust.stdlib_note: Only `std` (and `core`/`alloc`). No crates.io dependencies at all (no serde, no libc crate, no regex). If you need OS functionality std lacks (e.g. mmap, signals), declare the needed C functions yourself with `extern "C"` against the system libc.

python.toolchain: CPython 3.14 (`python3` on PATH is 3.14). No virtualenv or pip installs are possible or needed.
python.stdlib_note: Only the Python standard library (json, csv, http.server, socketserver, threading, concurrent.futures, mmap, zlib, struct, decimal, datetime, unittest, …). No third-party packages (no numpy, pandas, pyarrow, sqlite-based query execution is NOT allowed: the `sqlite3` module must not be used).

go.toolchain: Go 1.27.1 (`go` on PATH; GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off — no module downloads). Use a go.mod with no requirements.
go.stdlib_note: Only the Go standard library (net/http, encoding/json, encoding/csv, sync, context, hash/crc32, syscall, testing, …). No external modules, including golang.org/x/*.

common-lisp.toolchain: SBCL 2.6.9 (`sbcl` on PATH, /opt/sbcl) with ASDF (bundled). Build a standalone executable or a core image via the Makefile (e.g. `sb-ext:save-lisp-and-die`); `bin/polyquery` may also start sbcl with a prebuilt core.
common-lisp.stdlib_note: Only ANSI Common Lisp, SBCL's own extensions (sb-ext, sb-sys, sb-alien, sb-unix, sb-int, sb-impl, sb-thread, sb-kernel) and the contribs bundled with SBCL (asdf, uiop, sb-bsd-sockets, sb-posix, sb-concurrency, sb-rotate-byte, sb-md5, sb-cltl2, sb-introspect, sb-simd, sb-sprof, sb-rt). No Quicklisp, no third-party systems (no alexandria, cl-json, hunchentoot, cl-ppcre, bordeaux-threads).

x86_64-asm.toolchain: GNU assembler (binutils 2.42) driven by gcc 13.3 on the native x86-64 host (AMD Zen 5: AVX2, BMI2, POPCNT and AVX-512F/BW/VL/DQ are available). NASM is installed but the build uses GNU `as` (`.S` files, AT&T or `.intel_syntax noprefix`).
x86_64-asm.optional_simd: Optionally add a third variant `x86_avx512` (AVX-512F/BW/VL/DQ) — the host supports it.
x86_64-asm.bench_note: You can measure on the native x86-64 host (AMD Zen 5); timings are noisy because other jobs may run concurrently, so repeat measurements. An independent before/after measurement on a quiet host follows your run.
x86_64-asm.bench_done: and benchmark results from `make -C native-kernels bench` for the new kernels
x86_64-asm.optional_simd_opt: You may also optimize the optional `x86_avx512` variant.

arm64-asm.toolchain: aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3 cross toolchain (GNU as). There is NO native AArch64 hardware: tests run under qemu-aarch64 user-mode emulation (`make -C native-kernels test-cross`), which verifies correctness only — emulated timings are meaningless, do not report them as performance.
arm64-asm.abi: AAPCS64 (Procedure Call Standard for the Arm 64-bit Architecture)
arm64-asm.test_note: (AArch64 runs under qemu emulation: functional only)
arm64-asm.optional_simd: Optionally add a third variant `a64_sve` (SVE, vector-length agnostic); note that it can only be validated under emulation.
arm64-asm.bench_note: There is no native AArch64 hardware in your workspace and emulated timings are meaningless, so you cannot measure: reason from the target microarchitecture (Arm Cortex-X925 cores: 4 x 128-bit SIMD pipes, SVE2 with 128-bit vectors) and state the expected effect of each change. An independent before/after measurement on the native target follows your run.
arm64-asm.bench_table_note: (expected effects with your reasoning, since you cannot measure)
arm64-asm.optional_simd_opt: You may also optimize the optional `a64_sve` variant.
